name: Spicules
desc: The burning prairie — the sun's edge in H-alpha is not an edge but grass, a forest of chromospheric jets launched up the magnetic field, climbing, hanging and draining back down the same field line they came up, crowded into bushes along the network boundaries and combed over by the field while the disk below them streams with fibrils; in the doppler style the colour is the real observable, so the forest sorts itself into blue jets climbing toward you and red ones falling away.

energy.doc: how hard the rim is driven — jet height, launch rate, glow, off-limb scale height and the contrast of the fibrils on the disk (the master knob)

scale.doc: jet size and how close you are standing — at max a few enormous macrospicules cross the whole plate and the limb flattens out

speed.doc: time rate (0.15 climbs at something like the pace the real sun does it)

density.doc: how many jets, and how many network cells they bunch into — a sparse stubble of lone spikes or a solid seething prairie

lean.doc: prevailing field direction the forest is combed along — 0.5 is upright, either extreme lays the whole rim over on its side

hue.doc: H-alpha tone (8 = the scarlet of the real line); the ca_k and doppler styles set their own colour on purpose

x.doc: where the active plage sits along the rim — that stretch burns brighter and throws the tallest jets

y.doc: height of the limb in the frame — how much disk you see under the forest

style.doc: aesthetic: scarlet H-alpha limb / violet-white Ca II K with a hard bright network / inverted on-disk view where the jets are pure dark mottles absorbing the disk behind them, no interior at all / abstracted dopplergram — jets coloured by the sign of their line-of-sight velocity, blue climbing and red draining / sumi ink on warm paper

seed.doc: deterministic seed for jet placement, bushes, life phases, lean and bend
